mainTopic: Checking for purity during ימי זיבה and the seven clean days: backward impurity, וסת, and which checks count
overview: The גמרא first brings a ברייתא from לוי: a woman who skipped the proper check at the end of her נדה days is a ספק זבה, whatever a later check shows. It then asks whether the משנה's words 'she makes things impure for twenty-four hours' refute רבא, and answers that those words refer back to the girl at the start of the פרק. Next it asks whether 'if she has a וסת' refutes רב הונא בר חייא. He explains that his rule only means a וסת in ימי זיבה is uprooted after one miss. The חכמים then argue against רבי יהודה that a late check on day seven is no better than a check on day one. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון keep her pure with a clean check on any day back to day two, and רבי reasons that day one works too. A new משנה brings a three-way dispute about a זב or זבה who checked only on days one and seven. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about counting with gaps, and the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. The amud ends by opening a new question about checking on days one and eight, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: לוי's ברייתא supports the ruling
steps.stepSummary: לוי taught a ברייתא saying that if she checked only after several days, she is a ספק זבה whether that check came out pure or impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לוי taught the same thing in his ברייתא: after the days, whether she checked and found herself pure or checked and found herself impure, she is an uncertain זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from לוי that matches the ruling it was just discussing. It shows that this ruling has support from an outside source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case she never did a proper check to confirm that her נדה days were over, and she only checked later. The ברייתא says the result of the later check makes no difference: she is a ספק זבה either way. A clean check days later cannot prove she was clean during the days she skipped.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה; here, a ברייתא that לוי taught
After the days, meaning she checked only several days later
She checked herself for blood
A woman who may be a זבה; her status is uncertain

phrases.english: And so Levi taught in his baraita:
After the days,
phrases.notes: She skipped the proper check at the end of her נדה days and only checked later.

phrases.english: whether she examined and found herself pure
or whether she examined and found herself impure,
she is an uncertain zava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling the גמרא was discussing just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that a later check does not settle her status, so she remains a ספק זבה

steps.title: Does the משנה's twenty-four-hour line refute רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says she makes things impure for twenty-four hours. That seems to go against רבא, who says a woman does not do this during her ימי זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And she makes things impure for twenty-four hours.' Shall we say this is a refutation of רבא? For רבא said that a woman does not make things impure backward for twenty-four hours during her days of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה and asks whether it disproves a statement of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in our משנה is a woman who is in her ימי זיבה, and the משנה says she is מטמאה מעת לעת. רבא said the opposite: during ימי זיבה there is no twenty-four-hour backward impurity. If the משנה really means this woman, it clashes with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: She makes things she touched impure backward for the past twenty-four hours
Shall we say? It opens a suggested challenge
A strong refutation of a sage's opinion
Her days of זיבה, the eleven days between one נדה period and the next

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Seeing blood during the regular נדה time can bring the twenty-four-hour backward impurity. רבא is talking only about blood seen during ימי זיבה.

phrases.english: "And she transmits impurity for twenty-four hours."
Let us say this is a refutation of Rava!
For Rava said: this comes to say
that a woman does not transmit impurity for twenty-four hours
during her days of ziva!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the משנה and starts a new discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that there is no twenty-four-hour backward impurity during ימי זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה is about a woman in her ימי זיבה, and it says she is מטמאה מעת לעת.

steps.title: Didn't we already refute רבא once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it is raising a refutation against רבא as if it were new, when it already refuted him once before.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already raise a refutation against רבא one time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question its own wording. רבא was already refuted elsewhere, so why ask 'shall we say this refutes רבא' as if it were a fresh idea?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is not about the law itself. It is about how the challenge was worded. It sets up the next step, which explains what the challenge really means.

keyTerms.meaning: We raised a refutation against him
One time, once already

phrases.english: But didn't we raise a refutation against Rava
one time already!
phrases.notes: He means an earlier place in this מסכת where רבא was refuted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the challenge in step 2 was worded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the גמרא presents a refutation of רבא as new when he was already refuted

steps.title: This is another refutation of רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that it means: here is one more source that refutes רבא, besides the earlier one.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what we mean: shall we say there is a refutation of רבא from this source too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. It is not claiming this is the first refutation. It is saying our משנה would be a second one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 2 still stands, but now it is understood as an extra proof against רבא. This sets up the defense of רבא that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what we are saying, explaining what we meant
From this source too

phrases.english: This is what we are saying:
Let us say there is a refutation of Rava
from this as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The challenge means our משנה would be an additional refutation of רבא, not the first one.

steps.title: The twenty-four-hour line refers back to the start of the chapter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that 'she makes things impure for twenty-four hours' refers to the first משנה of the פרק, about the girl who saw blood while still in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא can tell you: when the משנה teaches 'she makes things impure for twenty-four hours,' it refers back to the beginning of our פרק, to the girl who saw blood while she was still in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. The twenty-four-hour line does not describe the woman in ימי זיבה; it belongs to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'מטמאה מעת לעת' is attached to the first משנה of the פרק, about a young girl who saw blood before her marriage. Once that special situation ends, she is treated like other women and becomes מטמאה מעת לעת. So our משנה never says that a woman in ימי זיבה is מטמאה מעת לעת, and רבא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It refers to the beginning of our פרק
She saw blood while still in her father's house, before her marriage

steps.whatToRemember: רבא survives this challenge. The משנה's twenty-four-hour rule goes back to the girl at the start of the פרק, not to a woman in ימי זיבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a line in a משנה can refer back to an earlier משנה. Reading it that way removes the clash with רבא's rule about ימי זיבה.

phrases.english: Rava can say to you:
when it teaches "she transmits impurity for twenty-four hours,"
it refers to the beginning of our chapter,
phrases.notes: This is the first משנה of the פרק, back on 64b.

phrases.english: to the girl who saw blood while still in her father's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבא from steps 2 and 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the משנה's phrase so that it refers to a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'מטמאה מעת לעת' described the woman in ימי זיבה in our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase refers to the girl at the start of the פרק, so it does not contradict רבא.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to teach this about the girl
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the משנה needed to say that the girl from the first משנה of the פרק makes things impure for twenty-four hours. Without it, we might have thought the pure days in between make each sighting a fresh start, with no backward impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since days of purity interrupt her sightings, each new sighting is like the start of her נדה, so she should not make things impure for twenty-four hours. The משנה teaches us that she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבא's answer from Step 5. It explains what new point the משנה teaches once we read it as talking about the girl in her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 moved the ruling 'she makes things impure for twenty-four hours' over to the girl case. Someone could ask why that needed saying. The answer: the pure days between her sightings might make us treat each sighting like a fresh first time. A fresh first time has no backward impurity, so the משנה has to tell us that here she still makes things impure for twenty-four hours.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken first idea the text comes to correct)
Days of purity, when blood she sees does not make her impure
The beginning of her נדה period, like a fresh start
For twenty-four hours back, meaning backward impurity on things she touched
It teaches us (this is the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבא's own rule. רבא still holds that a woman in her ימי זיבה does not make things impure for twenty-four hours. This step only explains why the משנה needed to teach the girl's case.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say
since pure days interrupt between them,
it is like the beginning of her נדה,
and she should not make things impure for twenty-four hours;
so it teaches us (that she does).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from Step 5 by showing the new point the משנה teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the משנה needed to say it (a 'you might have thought' explanation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because pure days separate her sightings, each sighting is like a fresh start of נדה, with no twenty-four-hour backward impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, the girl makes things impure for twenty-four hours, and the משנה needed to teach this.

steps.title: Does 'if she has a וסת' refute רב הונא בר חייא?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if she has a fixed cycle (וסת), her time is enough. That seems to assume a woman can have a וסת during her ימי זיבה, which goes against רב הונא בר חייא in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If she has a fixed cycle.' Shall we say this refutes רב הונא בר חייא in the name of שמואל? For he said in the name of שמואל that a woman does not set a fixed cycle during her days of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new phrase from the משנה and uses it to challenge רב הונא בר חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a leniency to a woman who has a וסת, and it is talking about a time that can fall in her ימי זיבה. רב הונא בר חייא, in the name of שמואל, said a woman cannot set a וסת during those days. If the משנה relies on a וסת there, his rule looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, regular time when a woman expects to see blood
Shall we say this is a refutation?
Sets (establishes) a fixed cycle
The eleven days after the נדה days, when blood can make her a זבה

phrases.english: "If she has a fixed cycle."
Shall we say this is a refutation

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: of רב הונא בר חייא, who said in the name of שמואל?

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל,
phrases.english: For רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל:

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה קוֹבַעַת לָהּ וֶסֶת בִּימֵי זִיבָתָהּ.
phrases.english: This is to say that a woman does not set a fixed cycle during her days of זיבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תִּהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new phrase in the משנה and opens a new challenge, now against a different אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בר חייא in the name of שמואל: a woman does not set a וסת in her ימי זיבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the leniency of a וסת during a time that can be ימי זיבה, so a וסת must be able to exist then.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חייא: his rule was only a leniency
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא answers that 'no וסת in ימי זיבה' only means such a וסת is uprooted after one time instead of three. A וסת can still exist then, and since her blood is 'removed' in those days, her time is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא can say to you: when we say a woman does not set a וסת in her days of זיבה, we mean she does not need three times to uproot it. We say her blood is removed in those days. And since her blood is removed, her time is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא defends himself by explaining what his rule really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a וסת is uprooted only after it fails three times. In the ימי זיבה we assume her normal blood is 'removed' (not expected), so a וסת there is weak and one miss uproots it. That same idea is a leniency: since blood is not expected, when she does see, she is impure only from that moment, which fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To uproot, meaning to cancel a fixed cycle
Three times (the usual number of misses needed to uproot a וסת)
Her blood is removed: we don't expect her to see blood then
Her time is enough: she is impure only from when she saw, not backward

steps.whatToRemember: In the ימי זיבה a וסת is weak: one miss uproots it. But because blood is not expected then, a woman who does see is impure only from that moment (דיה שעתה).
steps.whyThisMatters: One idea, 'her blood is removed', works in two directions: it makes a וסת easy to cancel, and it saves her from backward impurity.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: רב הונא בר חייא can say to you:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן אֵין אִשָּׁה קוֹבַעַת לָהּ וֶסֶת
phrases.english: When we say a woman does not set a fixed cycle
during her days of זיבה,
we mean that she does not need three times to uproot it,
because we say her blood is removed;
and since her blood is removed,
her time is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the meaning of the challenged rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No וסת in ימי זיבה' meant a וסת cannot exist there at all, which would clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means one miss uproots such a וסת. Since her blood is removed, דיה שעתה, which agrees with the משנה.

steps.title: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to רבי יהודה's opinion in the משנה. It brings a ברייתא where the חכמים start to argue with him: his view would make sense only if she kept checking herself through the whole twilight.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'רבי יהודה says.' It was taught in a ברייתא: They said to רבי יהודה: if her hands were placed in her 'eyes' the entire twilight, what you say would be fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה from the משנה and brings the start of the חכמים's argument against him. This sets up the rest of their argument, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי יהודה says that a woman who did not check from מנחה time on her seventh day is treated as impure. The חכמים answer that this would only be fair if the law required her to keep checking all through בין השמשות. The line opens their argument, and the next step gives their full point.

keyTerms.meaning: If only; if it were so
Twilight, the doubtful time between day and night
What you say is fine (it would make sense)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Her eyes' here is a polite way of talking about the place where she checks for blood. It does not mean her actual eyes.

phrases.english: "רבי יהודה says."
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, where רבי יהודה says she is impure if she did not check from מנחה time on.

phrases.english: It was taught: They said to רבי יהודה:
If her hands were placed in her 'eyes'
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying she would be checking herself the whole time.

phrases.english: the entire twilight,
what you say would be fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new part of the משנה (רבי יהודה's opinion) and begins a new argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that a woman who did not check from מנחה time on is presumed impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His strictness would only be fair if she had to keep checking all through twilight, and she does not have to.

steps.title: The חכמים finish their argument: a late check is no better than a first-day check
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים complete their challenge to רבי יהודה. If we worry she saw blood the moment she stopped checking, then a check at מנחה time on day seven is no better than a check on day one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But now that you say a morning check is not enough, you must be worried that right as she took her hand away she saw blood. If so, what difference does it make whether she checked herself into purity on the seventh day from מנחה time and later, or on the first day?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים finish the argument they began in the last step. They show that רבי יהודה's worry, taken seriously, makes his own rule pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה requires a clean check late on day seven, from מנחה time onward. The חכמים say that unless she checks through the whole of בין השמשות, there is always a gap after her last check. So a late afternoon check leaves a gap just like a first-day check does, and his line between them does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Right as she took her hand away, meaning the moment she finished checking
She 'separated in purity': a clean check that marks her move from impurity to purity
From the time of מנחה, the late afternoon, and onward

phrases.english: But now, you must be saying:
phrases.notes: The חכמים are still talking to רבי יהודה, continuing from 'if she kept checking through the whole twilight.'

phrases.english: right as she took her hands away, she saw blood?
If so, what difference is it to me if she checked herself into purity
on the seventh day, from מנחה time and later,
or what difference is it to me if she checked herself into purity on the first day?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַכְשָׁיו אֵימַר: עִם סִלּוּק יָדֶיהָ רָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the חכמים's argument against רבי יהודה that began in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that she must check in purity from מנחה time onward on day seven
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His worry about a gap after the last check applies to any check that does not run through all of בין השמשות. So a late check and a first-day check are equally weak, and his distinction falls apart.

steps.title: Does anyone really say a first-day check is enough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks up the חכמים's mention of 'the first day' and asks whether anyone actually holds that a check on the first day is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day? Is there anyone who says that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about the words 'on the first day.' It wants to know whether any opinion really says a check on day one is enough to keep her pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים in the משנה said 'even on the second day.' So when the ברייתא has them speak of the first day, it sounds like they go further than the משנה. The גמרא asks if that position really exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone who says this? A question asking whether an opinion really exists
On the first day of her seven נדה days

phrases.english: On the first day?
phrases.notes: This picks up the last words of the חכמים's argument in the step before.

phrases.english: Is there anyone who says that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one detail, 'on the first day,' from the חכמים's argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether any תנא really holds that a clean check on the first day alone is enough.

steps.title: Yes: רבי asked רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון about a woman who checked only on the morning of day seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and brings a ברייתא. רבי asked רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון about a נדה who checked clean only on the morning of day seven. They said she keeps her status of purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי said, I asked רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון while they were walking on the road: a נדה checked herself on the morning of the seventh day and found herself pure, but she did not check at twilight. Days later she checked and found herself impure. What is the law? They told him: she keeps her status of purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a ברייתא. In it, רבי asks two great sages about a woman who skipped the late check on day seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case רבי יהודה worries about: no check at בין השמשות. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון rule that she is still treated as pure until she finds blood. This step sets up the follow-up questions about earlier days, which is where the 'first day' answer is heading.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman made impure by her period, now counting her days toward purity
In the morning
In a status of purity: we assume she is pure until we know otherwise

phrases.english: Yes, as a ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: רבי said: I asked רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון
while they were walking on the road:

phrases.aramaic: נִדָּה שֶׁבָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי שַׁחֲרִית
phrases.english: A נדה who checked herself on the seventh day in the morning
and found herself pure,
but at twilight she did not check herself into purity,

phrases.aramaic: וּלְאַחַר הַיָּמִים בָּדְקָה וּמָצְאָה טְמֵאָה — מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and after some days she checked and found herself impure: what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לִו: הֲרֵי זוֹ בְּחֶזְקַת טׇהֳרָה.
phrases.english: They said to him: she keeps her status of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, וְהָתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 11's question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, such an opinion exists. The ברייתא shows רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון keep her pure even without a check at בין השמשות, and the follow-up questions move to earlier days.

steps.title: Earlier days are no different
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks about a check on the sixth, fifth, fourth, third or second day. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון answer that it makes no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: What if it was the sixth, fifth, fourth, third or second day? They said to him: it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes the question back day by day. The sages answer that a clean check on any of these earlier days still keeps her in her status of purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new question moves the clean check further from the end of the seven days, and each time the answer stays the same. The list is working back toward the first day, which is what the גמרא needed to show that some sages say an early check is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is no different: the same law applies

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים argue against רבי יהודה that without checking through all of בין השמשות there is always a gap, so a late check is no better than an early one. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון rule that a clean check on day seven, and even on earlier days, keeps her pure until she finds blood.

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשִּׁי, חֲמִישִׁי, רְבִיעִי, שְׁלִישִׁי, שֵׁנִי — מַאי?
phrases.english: What if it was the sixth, fifth, fourth, third or second day?
phrases.notes: He means: what if her only clean check was on one of these days instead of day seven?

phrases.english: They said to him: it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשִּׁי, חֲמִישִׁי, רְבִיעִי, שְׁלִישִׁי, שֵׁנִי — מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, extending the ruling to earlier days.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A clean check on any earlier day also leaves her in her status of purity. This builds toward the first day the גמרא asked about.

steps.title: רבי admits he should have asked about the first day too
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he made a mistake by not asking about a check on the first day. His reasoning: on every day she starts out presumed impure, yet one clean check shows the bleeding stopped. The same should be true for day one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: I did not ask about the first day, and I was wrong not to ask. On all the other days she is also presumed impure, and still, once a check shows the bleeding stopped, we say it stopped. So on the first day as well, once it stopped, it stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes the ברייתא by saying he should have asked about day one as well. He gives a logical argument that a clean check on day one should also work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On days two through seven she is still presumed impure, yet one clean check is enough to show that the flow has stopped. Day one is no different, because it is the same kind of check. This completes the answer to step 11: yes, there is a view that a check on the first day is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: I made a mistake
Is that to say? (introduces a rhetorical point)
a presumed status of impurity
once it stopped, it stopped (a clean check ends the flow)

phrases.english: About the first day I did not ask,
and I made a mistake by not asking.
Is that to say that all of them are not
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the other days רבי did ask about, from day two to day seven.

phrases.english: standing in a presumed status of impurity?
And yet once it stopped, it stopped.
phrases.notes: "It" is the bleeding. A clean check shows it stopped.

phrases.english: The first day too:
once it stopped, it stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹן לֹא שָׁאַלְתִּי, וְטָעִיתִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁאַלְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. After hearing that days two through six all work, רבי applies the same logic to day one.
steps.raayaObject: That a clean check on the first day alone is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: A סברא: every day starts with a presumption of impurity, yet a clean check still shows the flow stopped, so day one works the same way
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof for step 11. There really is a view that a check on the first day is enough.

steps.title: Why did רבי first avoid asking about day one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי was thinking at first, when he chose not to ask about the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And at first, what did he think?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי left out the first day in the first place. This question sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי now says day one is like all the other days. So there must have been some reason he first treated it differently, and the גמרא wants to know what it was.

keyTerms.meaning: at first, originally
what did he think? what was his reasoning?

phrases.english: And at first, what did he think?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רבי's original reasoning, which he took back in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason רבי first had for treating the first day differently

steps.title: On day one the flow had just been flowing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי first thought day one was different, because she had just been bleeding and was presumed to have an open flow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since she was presumed to have an open spring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's first thought. Right after bleeding, her body is presumed to still be flowing, so a check on that day might not prove much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On day one the bleeding has only just ended, so she is strongly presumed to still be flowing. That is why רבי first doubted that a single clean check could overturn it. In the end he decided that a clean check still shows the flow stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: since, because
was established, was presumed
an open spring, meaning the flow from the womb is still active

phrases.english: Since she was presumed to have an open spring.
phrases.notes: The "spring" is the source of the blood, the womb. On day one it was just flowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At first רבי thought day one was weaker because the flow had just been active (מעין פתוח), so a single check might not be trusted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון ruled that one clean check on day seven, or on any day back to day two, keeps her presumed pure. רבי reasons that the same is true even for the first day, so there is a view that a first-day check is enough. He first hesitated about day one only because the flow had just been active.

steps.title: משנה: a זב and זבה who checked only on day one and day seven
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a זב or זבה checked clean on day one and day seven but not in between. רבי אליעזר says they are pure. רבי יהושע says only days one and seven count. רבי עקיבא says only day seven counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A זב and a זבה who checked themselves on the first day and found clean, and on the seventh day and found clean, but did not check on the days in between. רבי אליעזר says: they are presumed pure. רבי יהושע says: they have only the first day and the seventh day. רבי עקיבא says: they have only the seventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a three-way dispute about a זב or זבה who skipped the checks on days two through six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר says the two clean checks cover the whole week, so all seven days count. רבי יהושע says only the two days that were actually checked count, so five more days are needed. רבי עקיבא says only day seven counts, so six more days are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with a discharge who must count seven clean days
a woman with bleeding outside her regular time who must count seven clean days
a presumed status of purity
in between
only

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does not say they are impure. He says only two of the seven days count, so they still need five more clean days.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A zav and a zava,
who checked themselves on the first day
phrases.notes: These are the seven clean days a זב or זבה must count before going to the מקוה.

phrases.english: and found themselves clean,
and on the seventh day, and found themselves clean,
but on the rest of the days in between they did not check:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
They are presumed pure.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
They have only the first day
and the seventh day.
phrases.notes: He means only these two days count toward the seven, so five more are needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם אֶלָּא יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי בִּלְבָד.
phrases.english: They have only the seventh day.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזָּב וְהַזָּבָה, שֶׁבָּדְקוּ עַצְמָן בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּמָצְאוּ טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is related to the previous topic of checking during clean days, but now the case is a זב or זבה with checks on day one and day seven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: fully pure. רבי יהושע: only days one and seven count. רבי עקיבא: only day seven counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute shapes the rest of the סוגיא, which works out the reasoning behind each of the three views.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: you cannot count the seven days with gaps
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי אליעזר challenges רבי יהושע. Counting day one and day seven but not the days between means counting with gaps, but the תורה requires the seven days to come one after another with no impurity in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: רבי אליעזר said to רבי יהושע: According to you, you are counting with gaps. But the תורה said "after that she shall be pure," which means after all of them, so that no impurity separates between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר attacks רבי יהושע's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע counts day one and day seven but not the days between them, so his count has holes in it. רבי אליעזר reads "אחר תטהר" to mean purity comes only after seven days in a row, with no impure days breaking them up. So רבי יהושע's middle position cannot work.

keyTerms.meaning: according to your words, according to your view
with gaps, not one after another
"after that she shall be pure" (the פסוק about counting seven days)
separates, breaks up

phrases.english: Gemara: It was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to Rabbi Yehoshua:
According to your words, you are counting with gaps,
but the Torah said, "after that she shall be pure,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:28

phrases.english: "after" means after all of them,
so that no impurity separates between them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: לִדְבָרֶיךָ, אַתָּה מוֹנֶה בְּסֵירוּגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה with a ברייתא that challenges רבי יהושע's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling that days one and seven count while the days between do not
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק "אחר תטהר" requires seven days in a row with no impurity breaking them up. Counting day one and day seven with unchecked days between them is counting with gaps, which the תורה does not allow.

steps.title: רבי יהושע shows that counting with gaps already exists
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers רבי אליעזר: you yourself agree that a זב who had a קרי, and a נזיר who walked under overhanging branches, count with gaps, even though the תורה wants the days in a row.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: And you, don't you agree about a זב who had a seminal emission, and about a נזיר who walked under overhanging branches and jutting parts, that he counts with gaps? And the תורה said: 'And the earlier days shall be lost.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע defends himself against רבי אליעזר's challenge by pointing to two cases where even רבי אליעזר lets someone count with gaps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said the seven days must come one after another with nothing in the middle. רבי יהושע answers that in the case of a זב who had a קרי, and a נזיר who passed under doubtful branches, only one day is lost and the counting picks up again, so there is a gap. That happens even though the תורה speaks of earlier days being lost for a נזיר, which sounds like everything must start over.

keyTerms.meaning: A seminal emission; a different kind of impurity from זיבה
Overhanging tree branches and jutting parts of walls, which may be covering something impure
Shall fall away, meaning the earlier days are lost and do not count

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
And you, don't you agree
about a zav who had a seminal emission,
phrases.notes: He means it happened during his seven clean days.

phrases.english: and about a nazirite who walked under overhanging branches and jutting parts,
phrases.notes: There might be a dead body underneath, so it is only a doubt whether he became impure.

phrases.english: that he counts with gaps?
And the Torah said:
"And the earlier days shall be lost."
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's challenge from step 18 by showing that counting with gaps is accepted elsewhere.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-example: cases where everyone agrees counting with gaps works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven days must be fully in a row, so day one and day seven cannot count without the days between.
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting with gaps is already accepted for a זב with קרי and for a נזיר under doubtful branches, so it is not impossible.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר rejects the example of the זב who had a קרי
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק teaches that a קרי cancels only its own day for a זב, and nobody will confuse a קרי with real זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר? He would say: It makes sense there, because the Merciful One said 'to become impure by it,' meaning a קרי cancels only its own day. And if you worry people will confuse a זב with someone who had a קרי, they will not confuse them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אליעזר answers the first example, the זב who had a קרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a זב, a פסוק itself says that a קרי only cancels that one day, so a gap there comes straight from the תורה. And there is no fear that people will mix this up with a real flow of זיבה, which restarts the count, because the two are clearly different.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; granted that this case works
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Cancels; undoes the days already counted
To mix up; to confuse one case with another

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer?
It makes sense there,
because the Merciful One said "to become impure by it" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:32

phrases.english: meaning it cancels only its own day,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מִשּׁוּם אִיחַלּוֹפֵי זָב בְּבַעַל קֶרִי —
phrases.english: and if you worry that people will confuse a zav with one who had a seminal emission —
they will not be confused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the first of רבי יהושע's two examples.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the זב-with-קרי example as a proof
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That gap comes from a פסוק, and the cases are too different to be confused, so it says nothing about our case.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר rejects the example of the נזיר under the branches
steps.stepSummary: The impurity of the branches is only a rabbinic rule, and people will not confuse a rabbinic rule with a תורה rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נזיר who walked under overhanging branches and jutting parts is also no proof. By תורה law we need a real tent over the dead body; it was the רבנן who made a decree here. And people will not confuse a rabbinic rule with a תורה rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with רבי אליעזר's answer, now dealing with the second example, the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, impurity passes under a cover only if it is a proper tent, and branches are not one. So the נזיר's impurity is only a rabbinic decree, and the רבנן were lenient and let him lose only one day. Nobody will think that leniency also applies when he became impure by תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: By תורה law
A proper, full tent that spreads impurity from a dead body
Made a decree; a rule added by the רבנן

phrases.aramaic: נָזִיר שֶׁהִילֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי סְכָכוֹת וּפְרָעוֹת נָמֵי,
phrases.english: A nazirite who walked under overhanging branches and jutting parts is also no proof,
because by Torah law we need a proper tent,
and it was the Rabbis who made a decree,
and a rabbinic rule will not be confused with a Torah rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיר שֶׁהִילֵּךְ עַל גַּבֵּי סְכָכוֹת וּפְרָעוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אליעזר's answer, now handling the second example.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the נזיר example as a proof
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That impurity is only rabbinic, and a rabbinic leniency will not be confused with a תורה case.

steps.title: Why our case is different: a doubt could be confused with a certainty
steps.stepSummary: With the זבה who checked only on days one and seven, letting a doubtful day count might lead people to count it even when she surely saw blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, if we worry that perhaps she saw blood, then a doubtful case might be confused with a certain case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אליעזר's answer by showing why our case is not like the two examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהושע only worries that she might have seen blood in the middle days, he still lets day one count. But then people might also count day one when she definitely saw blood in between, which is wrong. So unlike the זב and the נזיר, here there is a real risk of mixing up the rules, and רבי אליעזר will not allow counting with gaps.

keyTerms.meaning: We worry; we are concerned about a possibility
A doubt; we do not know what happened
A certainty; we know it happened

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's answer: the זב with a קרי and the נזיר under branches lose only one day, but they cannot be mixed up with other cases. Our זבה case can be, because a doubt might be confused with a certainty.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אליעזר denies that the זב and the נזיר count with gaps. He agrees they do; he only says those cases cannot teach us anything about this one.

phrases.english: But here —
phrases.notes: Back to the זבה who checked only on day one and day seven.

phrases.english: if we worry that perhaps she saw blood,
a doubtful case will come to be confused with a certain case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אליעזר's answer by contrasting our case with the two examples.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהושע's whole comparison to the זב and the נזיר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In our case a doubtful day could be confused with a day she surely saw blood, a risk the other cases do not have.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא sounds most logical, but the ruling follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון rank the three opinions. רבי אליעזר sounds better than רבי יהושע, and רבי עקיבא sounds better than both. Still, the practical הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: רבי אליעזר's view seems more correct than רבי יהושע's, and רבי עקיבא's view seems more correct than all of them. But the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the final word on the debate about the זבה who checked herself only on days one and seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate judgments here. One is about which opinion sounds most logical, and רבי עקיבא, the strictest, wins that. The other is the practical ruling, and that goes to רבי אליעזר, who treats all seven days as clean.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of ... seem more correct (a judgment about logic, not a final ruling)
The practical law follows ...

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of the זבה who checked herself on days one and seven, רבי עקיבא's view sounds most logical, but in practice the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "seems more correct" with "the הלכה is like." The ברייתא openly says the view that sounds most logical, רבי עקיבא's, is not the one we follow in practice.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
The words of Rabbi Eliezer seem more correct
than the words of Rabbi Yehoshua,
and the words of Rabbi Akiva seem more correct than the words of all of them,
but the law follows Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, this ברייתא closes the debate and gives the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's view sounds most logical, but the practical הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Setting up a new question: checking on day one and day eight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question about a זב or זבה who checked themselves on the first day and the eighth day and found themselves clean, but did not check on the days in between. The actual question comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: a זב or זבה who checked themselves on day one and on day eight and found themselves clean, but did not check on the other days...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question by describing the case. It has not asked the question yet; that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is different from the משנה's case. There the person checked on day one and day seven, inside the seven clean days. Here the second check is on day eight, after the seven days are over, so day seven itself was never checked.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised among the חכמים, an open problem the גמרא will try to solve
A man or woman who became impure through a זיבה discharge and must count seven clean days
They checked themselves to confirm there was no discharge
The eighth day, the day after the seven clean days end

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
A zav and a zava who examined themselves
on the first day and on the eighth day
phrases.notes: Notice it says the eighth day, not the seventh. So day seven itself was never checked.

phrases.english: and found themselves pure,
but did not examine themselves on the rest of the days,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ruling on checking days one and seven is settled, the גמרא opens a new related case in which the second check was on day eight.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case is set up here: checking on days one and eight, with nothing checked in between. The question about how this counts continues in the next lines.
